title.narrative: Emergency Response to the flood-affected population in Umbada Locality, Khartoum, and Al-Salam Local

description.narrative:
Heavy rains and flash floods continue to affect tens of thousands of people across Sudan. By 23 August, the estimated number of people affected was 156,300, according to the Government’s Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC), humanitarian organisations on the ground, and local authorities. Torrential rains and floods destroyed at least 12,500 houses and damaged another 21,400 in 15 out of the 18 states. Government authorities reported that 83 people died and 30 people were injured since the beginning of the rainy season. In addition, the floods have reportedly affected at least 238 health facilities, 1,560 water sources, and over 1,500 latrines that have been damaged or washed away. People have lost over 330 heads of livestock, and over 5,200 feddans (21.84 km2) of agricultural land were affected by floods, which will contribute to already worrying levels of food insecurity. According to the assessment conducted on 24th Aug 2022 by CAFOD and HAC in coordination with other agencies, Umbada locality, Khartoum, is one of the worst affected areas that needs urgent emergency support. The team presented the data as shown in the table below. Among the other affected localities, Alsalam locality, White Nile is one of the localities affected by floods yearly. It consists of 5 administrative units (Miginis, Rawat, Naeim, Umjalala, and Zilit ), and among them, Al Rawat is the worst affected.
